{"kind": "fence"}], "rationale": "C is computed as 5 column-tiles of 16 rows (m=80, n=16), each needing two K-chunk products (k=32 = 2x16) accumulated in increasing K order: first compute overwrites the accumulator tile, second accumulates. The 32-row scratchpad holds exactly one 16-row A tile plus one 16-row B tile at a time, so B tiles cannot both stay resident alongside A. To minimize DMA input bytes, C tiles are processed in pairs with the two 16-row accumulator tiles: one B0 load serves the chunk-0 computes of two consecutive C tiles (B0 persists in scratchpad rows 16-31 across both), then one B1 load serves both chunk-1 computes. With only two accumulator tiles, at most two chunk-0 computes can use one B0 load before an accumulate+mvout must free an accumulator, so B0 and B1 each need ceil(5/2)=3 loads: 6 B mvins = 1536 bytes, provably minimal. All 10 distinct A tiles are loaded exactly once (2560 bytes, no waste since 80x32 splits into 5x2 exact 16x16 tiles). Total mvin traffic = 4096 bytes. A stream stride 32 bytes (A rows), B stream stride 16 bytes (B rows), store stride 64 bytes (16 int32 per C row). out_addr uses bit31 (accumulator space) + bit29 (full 32-bit width) + bit30 set only for the accumulate-stage preloads, low bits 0 or 16 for the two accumulator tiles; all computes use accumulated=false with the B tile staged by the immediately preceding preload, and bd_spad_addr=GARBAGE_ADDR as required. 46 commands total, final fence included."}
